current.text: Walker Kessler is gone from Utah. He was traded.
The projected starting lineup is Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic.
Nurkic is expected to start at center.
Ace Bailey is not expected to start now that Jackson Jr., Markkanen and George are healthy.
Kyle Filipowski and Jaxson Hayes are very unlikely to start. Jackson Jr. is not expected to play center full time.
Jackson Jr. is not a passer, which helps Nurkic as a passing center.
New arrivals include Darryn Peterson, Jaxson Hayes, Mo Bamba, Josh Okogie, Trey Alexander and Harrison Ingram. Jaren Jackson Jr. is available for a full season.
The roster is deep and the frontcourt is crowded. George, Peterson, Sensabaugh, Bailey, Markkanen and Jackson Jr. leave little room for Isaiah Collier.
Usage is crowded. Markkanen, George, Jackson Jr. and Peterson will all lose some touches. Rookies get less usage here.
Scoring should be balanced. Three or four players could top 20 points per game, but no one is expected to reach a career high in points.
Utah is trying to win this season and is not tanking. Fears that it will tank, shut players down or sit Markkanen are misplaced.
Experts expect a good team that probably makes the playoffs. Leaf projects 43 wins and a 7th or 8th seed. The market win total of 35.5 is lower than this view.
Because Utah plans to compete, the late-season minutes that young players got last season will not be available.
Utah is expected to have a top 10 offense and a defense ranked below 20th. Some zone defense is expected because the team has size.
Coach Will Hardy had a long leash during the tank years. He will feel pressure to tinker and win this season.
Utah has the fewest back-to-backs in the league, so its players have less rest risk.
The fantasy playoff schedule is about average: 10 games in weeks 19 to 21, with only 3 games in week 19.

durable.text: Utah has a strong home-court advantage from the crowd and the altitude.

note: Utah plans to win this season, and experts see little tank or shutdown risk. That protects Markkanen, Jackson Jr. and Nurkic through our playoffs, and the team has the fewest back-to-backs in the league. With four players sharing the ball, George, Markkanen and rookie Peterson each lose some touches, and bench players like Bailey, Collier and Filipowski have little room. Nurkic gains as the expected starting center and passer now that Kessler is gone. Early on, watch whether Nurkic holds the starting job and how Hardy splits minutes in the crowded frontcourt.
